title: What If EVERY Car in Your City Were Electric? 🏙️⚡ #shorts

scenes.text: What if every car in your city went electric overnight? Three things change. One surprise stays.
First, noise. Below about thirty-five miles an hour, streets get much quieter. At highway speed, tire roar dominates, so little changes.
Second, air. Tailpipe fumes vanish, right where people breathe.
The surprise: tires and brakes still shed fine dust. An OECD study found heavy long-range EVs emit a few percent more than gas cars. Lighter ones, a bit less.
Third, the grid. Electrifying every US passenger car needs about twenty-two percent more electricity. Spread out to twenty-fifty, that's about one percent a year.
EVs fix the tailpipe, not the tire. Should lighter cars be next? Follow EV Drive.
